newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Capital gain boosts profit at Belgian retailer GIB.
newsitem.headline: Capital gain boosts profit at Belgian retailer GIB.

text.p: Belgian retailer GIB Group said on Thursday a large capital gain sent its first-half 1996 profit soaring, and that full-year figures would show an improvement on 1995 levels.

A rise in full-year net profit and operating cashflow would be due mainly to better results at the group's GB Supermarkets division, which is undergoing restructuring, and its U.S. home-improvements chain Scotty's.
GIB's financial year ends on January 31.

First-half group net profit totalled 2.54 billion Belgian francs ($80.5 million) versus 645 million in the year ago period, pushed up by a previously-announced 1.86-billion franc capital gain on the sale of its minority stake in British home-improvement chain Homebase.
But without the capital gain profits were little changed from last year, a disappointment to analysts who were generally expecting a rise in current profit.

Consolidated turnover was 107 billion francs after 112 billion in first half 1995, but GIB said the two periods were not comparable because 1995 consolidated figures included its former loss-making U.S. unit Handy Andy.
First-half 1996 operating cashflow rose to 3.4 billion from 3.2 billion.
GIB is Belgium's second-largest retail group after Delhaize in terms of consolidated turnover.
Turnover at GB Supermarkets rose two percent versus first half 1995, with sales in food products rising three percent.

Productivity gains at GB translated into a "reinforced aggressive marketing policy" and by the end of the year GB would have renovated or enlarged 15 stores. The GB division had consolidated its market share and improved its results.

In its home-improvement divisions, sales at GIB's chains in Belgium, France, Spain and Portugal rose by 1.4 percent overall in the first half, though gardening equipment sales in Belgium and France suffered from poor weather.

Turnover at U.S. chain Scotty's climbed by six percent on the year-ago period, boosted by sales to professionals and its operating cashflow was higher. Scotty's continued its policy of opening small stores, with five new hardware shops so far this year and 17 more on the cards by the end of the year.

In its restaurant sector GIB was confident that despite disappointing results at beefburger-chain Quick Restaurants, in which GIB has a 57.44-percent stake, the fast-food market still had all its potential for development.

Quick had already announced the British "mad cow" scare had caused its first half sales to grow a less-than-expected- 11.8 percent in the first half, and had sent its profit plunging to seven million francs from 147 million.

Quick expected brand sales up between 10 and 12 percent for the year, and new products had been introduced to encourage customers to return. In the first half, 22 new restaurants were opened and 38 would be opened in the second half. ($1=31.54 Belgian Franc)
